summary: ORDER BY sorts the result, and LIMIT keeps only the first rows. Together they answer questions like top 3 or bottom 5.
notes: ORDER BY sorts ascending (ASC) unless you write DESC.
With two sort columns, the second one only breaks ties in the first.
SQLite puts NULL before every other value when sorting ascending. PostgreSQL puts NULL last, so add NULLS LAST or a WHERE gpa IS NOT NULL if it matters.
pitfall: Using LIMIT without ORDER BY gives you whichever rows the database reads first, not the top rows. Always sort before you limit.
